benchmarks.reference: Hand-built evaluation states in the tool-neutral vocabulary of SPEC-bidevaluation §13.1 (the §3.1 state object, optionally with a project-package document and a load/write action), covering the four §9 presets with their printed figures, every rule of the §5 table with at least one triggering case and one case that lists it absent, the boundary behaviour the spec states for the two thresholds (BID-R-031 fires on a strict '<' and BID-R-032 on a strict '>', so the exactly-equal cases are near-misses and use values that are exact in binary floating point), the degenerate weight geometries (a single row with omega_k = 1, zero-weight rows, a zero-weight row as the only critical one, dominance with x_crit = 100 %), ties at rank 1 and inside lower ranks, an edit of the published scoring table that reverses a rank, the two and ten bidder limits with their one-over near-misses, the §3.3 id derivations, the TQ drafts of §4.8 with their ids and default templates, and the package integration of §7 (explicit load, read mapping, ignored sections, an unknown top-level key, flags including an orphan, the write that replaces one item and leaves the others byte-identical, the collision and id-pattern refusals, and a write/resume round trip). Expected values were derived from the spec clause by clause and computed with an own standard-library Python implementation of §3.3 and §4.2-§4.8 (bidevaluation-ref.py beside this corpus, which regenerates this file and re-verifies every value against it); the sensitivity arithmetic is additionally checked against explicit 2^n vertex enumeration of the weight box and against the algebra of Triantaphyllou & Sanchez (1997) relation (8a). The external references are process context only: ISO 10845-1:2020 and Directive 2014/24/EU prescribe none of the numbers here, and no case claims conformity with either.

Bibliographic record verified 2026-09-22 from Crossref (doi 10.1111/j.1540-5915.1997.tb01306.x); the full text is paywalled, so the paper's printed Tables 2-5 are not re-read here and no case checks them. What is checked is the algebra the spec relies on: relation (8a) delta_{k,i,j} = (P_j - P_i)/(a_jk - a_ik), the relative form (6), and the 'robust criterion' notion.
Own reference implementation: bidevaluation-ref.py beside this corpus (standard library only; --spec reproduces every figure printed in spec §4.7 and §9.1-§9.4).
benchmarks.tolerance: Categorical outputs (verdict, sensitive, rule membership, finding counts, rank, knock-out state, provisional, challenger ids, draft ids and kinds, derived evaluation id, package_written, ignored sections) are exact: they are enumerations, integers, booleans or strings, and any difference is a logic difference. Numeric tolerances are taken from the arithmetic, not chosen to pass. score_pct and margin_pp: abs 1e-9 pp — §4.3 is a finite sum of products of user decimals, so only floating-point rounding separates two correct implementations (spec §13.2). delta_pp, critical_change_pp, x_crit_pct, pair_t_pct and r_pct: abs 1e-6 — each is a quotient of two float sums (§4.5 x* = -D_0/D_1 after two divisions by 1 - omega_k; §4.6 t_j = sum w d / sum w |d|), where a different but equally valid order of operations can move the last few ulps; 1e-6 is far below the 1e-4 printed rounding the spec's own acceptance criterion 5 uses and far above the ~1e-13 relative error the expressions can accumulate at these magnitudes. The two threshold boundaries are handled as spec §13.2 requires: the equality cases use dyadic values (|delta*| = 12.5 pp against threshold_pp 12.5; x_crit = 50 % against x_pct 50) that are exact in binary floating point, so the strict comparison is decided without tolerance.

The raw current-carrying-capacity columns (Table B.52.4 for A1-D2 and B.52.10/B.52.11 for method E) are copyrighted and could not be obtained from any source that reproduces them, so they are treated as an empirical data table: the whole table is read back out of the page and checked for integrity and monotonicity, the one value a public copy of the standard does show (A1, copper, 1,5 mm2 = 13,5 A) is checked exactly, and every copper column is checked against the published two-loaded-conductor Table B.52.2 through a physically bounded ratio. The aluminium columns and the buried D1/D2 columns have no independent source at all and are recorded as flagged, not passed.

benchmarks.tolerance: Agreement to the last digit the page prints: |got-ref| <= 0.5*10^-d + 1e-9*|ref|, with d = 1 decimal for the design current and the corrected ampacity (A), 0 decimals for the ampacity column of the candidate table, 2 decimals for voltage drop (%) and losses (kW), 3 decimals for every correction factor, 1 decimal for the adiabatic minimum section (mm2) and the short-circuit withstand (kA). Every graded quantity is a closed form on both sides, so the only physical slack is double-precision round-off. The ampacity table itself is an empirical data table and is not graded to a numeric tolerance: it is checked for integrity, for one exact primary-source value, and against a 0.82-0.96 (0.78-0.90 for method E) ratio band to the published two-loaded-conductor table with no cell more than 0.06 from its column median.

benchmarks.reference: Hand-built cause & effect matrices covering the five spec presets (P1-P5), a clean baseline and one trigger plus one near-miss for each of the 51 review rules CAU-R-001..091 (data validity, opposite-command and trip-versus-permissive conflicts, declared and derived exclusivity with the interval boundary rule and the M_i + M_j > N rule, coverage, safe state, latch and reset, voting independence by device key and by io controller/card/channel, energise/de-energise convention, io fail-state normalisation, bypass provisions, response-time budget, control_functions interlock resolution, analysis method switch at n = 16), scenario sequences for the channel/cause evaluation and the latch/reset acceptance predicate, display-to-SI conversion, matrix-id slug derivation, package item fields, ignored package sections, the mulberry32 check values and two seeded random matrices. Ten further cases (ids prefixed adj-) cover the points spec revision 2026-09-22.2 settled and the ungraded claims the second adjudication pass found. The first four: the spec 3.4 de_energised_state enum, an exclusive pair reached by both the declared and the derived route, the CAU-R-012 target order when the permissive cause is listed first, and the reset refusal reason when two conjuncts of the spec 4.3 predicate fail at once. Expected values were written by hand from SPEC-causeeffect.md rev 2026-09-22.2 and asserted against an own stdlib engine (causeeffect-ref.py); combination counts come from brute force over every subset evaluating the cells directly (spec 4.2), cross-checked against the pairwise count; sampled counts come from an own 32-bit port of mulberry32. Standards clauses are cited as the spec quotes them (IEC 61511-1:2016 10.3.2, 11.8.4, 11.8.5; IEC 61511-1:2003 3.2.45, 11.2.7, 11.6.2, 11.8.3; API RP 14C 7th ed. 4.3.3); the corpus author did not re-read the standard texts, so every rule reference here rests on the spec's formulas. The second pass added six: a bypassed cause that the review still counts (spec 4.4) while the scenario drops it; a 17-cause matrix with analysis.seed 7 and sample_count 1024 and a declared exclusive pair, so that the sampled branch is graded on a seed and a sample count other than the defaults and on rejecting infeasible samples; 'Fail Stopped' and 'stop' normalised to the spec 4.7 'stopped' row, triggering CAU-R-054 on a start effect and missing it on a stop effect; the scenario states running, energised and de-energised; preset P2 with its permissive cell removed, the acceptance-criterion-3 case for CAU-R-011; and the fourteen display units of spec 3.3.1 that conv-display-to-si does not reach.

benchmarks.reference: Analytic well-mixed limits (dT = P/(rho cp Q), C = C_out + S/Q) and the exact conservation identities, derived and implemented independently in python, plus the de Vahl Davis (1983) Table I cavity - which is itself re-derived here from the governing equations by an independent stream-function/vorticity solver on 41/61/81 grids, because cfd.html carries the same published table at line 4583.  This is deliberately NOT a comparison against high-fidelity CFD: the tool is a reduced-order voxel solver and is graded on the laws that must hold at any fidelity.

U. Ghia, K.N. Ghia, C.T. Shin, "High-Re solutions for incompressible flow using the Navier-Stokes equations and a multigrid method", Journal of Computational Physics 48 (1982) 387-411, Tables I and II (129x129 grid).  Carried, not executed.

benchmarks.tolerance: Conservation laws are graded tightly (1e-4 relative on the air balance, 2 % of gross turnover on the energy and tracer balances - the threshold the tool itself calls "good").  The well-mixed limits are graded with a 25 % allowance taken from ANSI/ASHRAE 62.1 Table 6-2 (air-distribution effectiveness 0.8-1.2), because the exhaust value is exact by balance while the VOLUME MEAN differs from it by the room's mixing quality.  The Boussinesq magnitude is graded at 15-25 % against de Vahl Davis on a coarse grid, a discretization window wide enough that only a genuinely wrong buoyancy coefficient fails.

benchmarks.reference: Pairwise-outcome corpus for a hazard-group chemical storage compatibility matrix. Each case lists a small inventory (name, physical state, CLP/GHS hazard statement codes, optional generic group meaning, optional location) and the expected matrix cell(s) in the README vocabulary X (prohibited together) / S (segregate) / U (unknown - review SDS) / C (no modelled conflict), or a boolean property (not C / not X) where the sources establish only that a pair reacts or must be separated. Expectations come from the CLP hazard-statement texts (EUH031/EUH032/EUH014/H26x/H27x), HSE HSG71 paras 71, 73, 120, the EPA-600/2-80-076 compatibility chart as transcribed by NIH ORF and Rutgers REHS and explained in WIPP Addendum B2, and the acceptance criteria of spec 11 / 00-common (unknown never safe, no inference from product name, symmetry, non-transitivity, rule id per cell, pack version in report). Stated mapping principle: fire, explosion, toxic/flammable gas or 'do not mix' -> X; heat or innocuous gas only -> S. Four randomized inventories (seed 20260916, n = 6/12/20/30) are generated by ref.py. 'group' values are generic meanings the harness maps to the tool's nearest group; null means no group chosen.

benchmarks.tolerance: All checks are categorical or integer and compared exactly: the tool is a rule engine with no numerical model, so there is no physical scale to set a tolerance from. Two non-scalar forms are used in the inventory cases: 'exact-subset' (every listed pair must have the stated cell; unlisted pairs are unconstrained because no source was read for them) and 'lower-bound' (count must be at least ref). Where the sources establish only a reaction or a separation duty, the check is the boolean 'not C' rather than a guessed X/S/U.

benchmarks.reference: ANSI/ANS-5.1-1979 fission-product decay-heat shape functions (23-term fits for thermal U-235, thermal Pu-239 and fast U-238); a generalised Bateman solution for branching decay chains implemented independently in 50-digit arithmetic and crosschecked against scipy.linalg.expm; the IAEA Nuclear Data Section evaluation of spontaneous-fission neutron yields; and ENSDF half-lives, Q values, branching ratios and mean decay energies retrieved from the IAEA Live Chart API.  Fission-product decay heat is carried against a SECOND, independent reference as well: direct summation over the ENDF/B-VIII.0 neutron-induced fission-yield sublibrary (England and Rider, ENDF-349) and the ENDF/B-VIII.0 decay sublibrary, the whole decay network solved from the independent yields.  Grading stays against ANS-5.1; the summation is recorded per case as the crosscheck, and the two references agree to better than 5 % on every one of the 65 decay-heat cases (worst ENDF/ANS = 0.9505 at 30 s after fast fission of U-238), so no case is excused on the grounds that the references disagree.  The Way-Wigner correlation is carried as an order-of-magnitude crosscheck only and is never graded.

benchmarks.tolerance: 5 % relative on fission-product decay heat against ANSI/ANS-5.1-1979.  That is one combined standard deviation: the standard is itself a fit whose evaluated uncertainty on f(t,T) is a few per cent, and the second independent reference used here - an ENDF/B-VIII.0 summation - itself sits 0 to 5 % below ANS-5.1 across these cases.  It is not chosen from the tool: it is the mutual spread of the two references, and two cases still fail it.  1e-6 relative on the decay solver against the closed-form Bateman solution, because that is exact mathematics and the two independent reference implementations agree to 3e-11.  1e-12 relative on the source-term identities, which are exact arithmetic within one call.  1 % on half-lives and 3 % on energy deposited per decay against ENSDF, which is the level at which an engineering decay library is normally rounded.  On spontaneous-fission neutron yields, the larger of 5 % and the 1 sigma the IAEA table quotes for that nuclide.

(34) and the IEC 60364-4-41 earth fault loop; the load flow is a scipy Newton solution of the complex nodal power balance, structurally different from the tool's backward/forward sweep. Every motor-free case is cross-checked against the analytic series path impedance Z = Z_source + sum(Z_branch), which is also verified by hand for case hand_single_feeder.

benchmarks.tolerance: Agreement to the last digit the page prints: |got-ref| <= 0.5*10^-d + 1e-9*|ref|, with d = 3 decimals for every kA/kappa figure in the selected-feeder panel, 2 decimals for current (A), voltage (V), voltage drop (%) and cable losses (kW), and 1 decimal for the source-current KPI. Both sides evaluate the same closed-form IEC 60909 expressions, so the only physical slack is double-precision round-off; the tolerance is set by the display, not by what makes the tool pass.

benchmarks.tolerance: Categorical outputs are exact: the fired set (rule id plus target), the verdict, the four severity counts, save_refused, candidate_id, the changed set, worst_case, max_flow_case, min_flow_case, next_rev and every integer count — all are discrete outcomes of boolean and string rules, so any deviation is a defect, not rounding. Numeric tolerances are derived from the arithmetic, not chosen to pass: si.<slot> carries relative 1e-12 because a stored value is one multiplication and one addition (SI = a x display + b) on the exact factors of spec 3.2, so about 2 ulp of double; RATING D/Req/margin_actual, NPSH diff, VALVE kv_req/phi/h, and BALANCE r carry relative 1e-9 (absolute 1e-9 when the reference is 0) because spec 13.2 sets that figure and because each is a closed-form chain of at most six double operations (a square root, two divisions, a logarithm), four orders of magnitude above their rounding. 1e-9 is also the tool's own comparison epsilon, so every boundary case here places its operands either exactly on the limit (40 degC against 40 degC, h = 0,10, r = 0,01, R = D, Um = 72 500 V, 1000 V, level 12 m = 12 m) or clearly off it (5e-9 and 5e-10 relative for the EQU-R-033 pair, 5e-9 and 5e-10 relative either side of the epsilon for EQU-R-033), never inside the epsilon band where the outcome would be a matter of rounding. Cases whose expected value depends on a disputable reading of the spec are marked disputable: true on the affected check and are listed in coverage.ambiguities.

citations: Derived in bench-src/ref/fourier_gen.py. The derived sets reproduce the standard results: square b_n=4/(n*pi) (n odd); sawtooth b_n=2(-1)^(n+1)/(n*pi); triangle b_n=8(-1)^((n-1)/2)/(pi^2 n^2) (n odd); duty-D pulse a_n=sin(2*pi*n*D)/(n*pi), b_n=(1-cos(2*pi*n*D))/(n*pi), mean=D; half-wave rectified sine mean=1/pi, b_1=1/2, a_2k=-(2/pi)/(4k^2-1).

benchmarks.provenance_note: Every one of the 235 closed-form cases carries a reference re-derived in python from NACA Report 1135, Shapiro Vol. I and Toro Ch. 4, implemented twice by structurally different routes and spot-checked against the published NACA 1135 Table I and Table II entries; no stored value was reused, so no case carries ref_source "recorded". The remaining 22 cases are not independent predictions and are labelled as such: the 4 unsteady-Euler cases assert conservation identities (mass and energy inventory drift, positivity repairs) plus a loose discretisation diagnostic, and the 18 nozzle internal-shock cases are a closure test -- the post-shock Mach, total-pressure loss, exit Mach and back pressure are re-derived from the pre-shock Mach the tool itself reports, so they prove the tool's internal-shock solution is self-consistent with the NACA 1135 relations, not that the shock is in the right place.
benchmarks.reference: Independent python re-derivation of the constant-gamma compressible-flow relations of NACA Report 1135 (isentropic, area-Mach, normal shock, theta-beta-M, Prandtl-Meyer), the Fanno and Rayleigh lines of Shapiro Vol. I, and the exact ideal-gas Riemann solver of Toro Ch. 4. Every relation is implemented twice by structurally different routes -- float64 closed forms with scipy brentq inversions, and a 60-digit mpmath second route that uses a different formulation wherever one exists (area ratio as a mass-flux ratio; the normal shock from raw mass/momentum/energy Rankine-Hugoniot balances; theta from the streamline density-ratio identity; Prandtl-Meyer and the Fanno friction function by numerical quadrature; Rayleigh T0/T0* assembled from p/p* and T/T*) -- and their mutual deviation is recorded as crosscheck. Spot-checked against the published NACA 1135 Table I and Table II entries.

benchmarks.tolerance: Two surfaces are compared for every closed-form case. (1) The value the tool DISPLAYS, against the tool's own printed precision: |got-ref| <= 0.5*10^-d + 1e-9*|ref|, where d is the number of decimals the tool actually prints for that field (5 for the area-table state ratios, 4 for Mach and pressure ratios, 3 for angles and for Mach numbers printed by the nozzle, 2 for u* and for times in ms, 1 for temperatures and wave speeds). (2) The UNROUNDED value the tool publishes through Diagram.record.build().outputs for the four closed-form modules (area / Fanno / Rayleigh / oblique-P-M), at 1e-9 relative -- these are closed forms the tool inverts with >=90 bisections over a bracket of order unity, so 1e-9 is loose for the tool and tight for the reference, with one derived exception: at the Rayleigh thermal-choking point T0/T0* has a quadratic maximum, so inverting it for the exit Mach is a square-root problem in which one ulp of the target moves M by ~2e-8; for those 14 cases `record_tol` states that arithmetic bound and the exact, well-conditioned assertion T0/T0*(M_reported) = 1 is tested instead, to 1e-12. Regime, branch and status labels are compared as strings, and every control write is verified to have landed. For the unsteady Euler cases the criterion is conservation: mass and energy inventory drift must read zero to the resolution the tool prints (3 decimals of a percentage, |drift| <= 5e-4 %) over a run with transmissive boundaries and no wave reaching an end wall; the L1 pressure error against the exact Riemann solution is a discretisation diagnostic with a loose 5% bound, not a physics tolerance. For the nozzle internal-shock closure cases the reference is a band: the tool prints the pre-shock Mach number to 3 decimals, so that +-0.0005 is propagated through the closure chain and the tool value must fall inside the resulting interval.

benchmarks.tolerance: Four bands, each fixed by the physics or by what the page prints, none by any step size. (1) Closed-form identities -- the ideal-gas state closure p = m R T / V and the density the page reports from it -- are exact arithmetic on both sides and are held to 1e-12 relative. (2) Marched quantities (terminal pressure, inventory, inventory change, inlet flow, peak inlet flow, terminal instant) are held to 1e-5 relative: that is two orders inside what the page prints (line pressures to 0.01 bar, about 2.5e-4 relative at its own default) and four orders inside the 12.6 % density error the declared ideal-gas closure itself carries at the default 60 bar supply (CoolProp 8.0 methane, Z = 0.8880). (3) The window-invariance families are held to a 1e-6 relative spread: the terminal answer is a property of the line, the gas and the two boundary flows, and the simulated-time window is not one of them, so the only admissible spread is residual discretisation noise. (4) The line pressure may never exceed max(p0, p_supply); that is a hard consequence of having no reverse flow and no heat input, and carries round-off slack only.

benchmarks.reference: The same coupled ODE system (CO2, O2, water vapour, trace contaminants, temperature, and the five accumulators) re-implemented independently in python from the model description and from the rate constants, crew rates and device characteristics read out of the page, integrated with scipy.integrate.solve_ivp (LSODA, rtol 1e-11, saturation handled as a constrained sub-system through a terminal event) — a different integrator family from the page fixed-step RK4. Grading is completed by invariants that owe nothing to either integration: the carbon and oxygen balances over the whole run, the analytic steady temperature, the ideal-gas closure, non-negativity, and the observed order of the scheme under step halving.
citations: scipy 1.17.1, scipy.integrate.solve_ivp (LSODA: Adams/BDF with automatic stiffness switching and local error control) — the independent integrator.

The rate constants, crew metabolic rates and device characteristics are the page's own, read out of the file, so that the benchmark grades the mathematics rather than the choice of physiological data.

Data provenance of those rates, checked separately: NASA/SP-2010-3407/REV1 Human Integration Design Handbook and NASA Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD, NASA/TP-2015-218570) give per crew member and day: 0.835 kg O2 consumed, 1.0 kg CO2 produced (respiratory quotient 0.87), about 1.9 kg metabolic water vapour and 2.5 kg drinking water; ASHRAE Standard 62.1 uses about 0.0052 L/s (19 L/h) of CO2 per sedentary adult.

Fourth-order Runge-Kutta truncation behaviour: E. Hairer, S. P. Norsett, G. Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations I, 2nd ed., Springer 1993, ch. II.1-II.3 (order conditions and the (h^4) global error of the classical scheme).
benchmarks.tolerance: Every displayed quantity is graded at 1e-7 relative plus a small absolute floor per quantity (1e-5 ppm CO2, 1e-7 kPa, 1e-6 K, 1e-6 % RH) for the near-zero cases. That is two orders of magnitude above the deviation actually observed against the adaptive reference (1e-9 or better) and two orders below anything that could reach the digits the page prints, so it grades the integration rather than the display. Carbon and oxygen balances are graded at 1e-9 relative for a sealed compartment, since the accumulators the page itself reports must close those balances exactly. The analytic steady temperature is graded at 0.02 K. The run at the step the page chooses must be step-converged: refining the step 16-fold must not move any displayed quantity by more than 1e-9 relative. The observed order of the scheme, measured where truncation is still visible (a reduced case with only the slow gas modes, steps of 225 s to 7200 s), must lie between 3.5 and 4.5. The saturated branch is the exception: there the surplus vapour is projected onto the saturation curve at the end of every step, which is a first-order splitting (measured order 1.00 over five halvings), so the saturating case is graded at 1e-4 relative — the deviation actually measured at the 10 s step the page uses is 1.8e-5 relative on the vapour pressure, 4.6e-5 K on the temperature and 1.3 g in 203 kg of condensate, three orders of magnitude below the resolution of anything the page prints — and the case additionally requires that deviation to fall linearly with the step, which is what proves the splitting consistent with the constrained solution.

benchmarks.tolerance: Categorical outputs are exact: verdict, package_savable, the finding map (rule@target -> severity), per-rule finding counts, severity counts, letter-code parses with their expected sets, address strings, the sorted unallocated list, and every integer count (n, c, V, C_req, C, channels, allocated, spare, cards, racks_required, counts by controller and signal type). spare_frac is compared to absolute 1e-12: it is the ratio of two integers computed by one division, so the only error is the final rounding. NE 43 values are compared to relative 1e-9 with an absolute floor of 1e-9*span, the tolerance spec 13 states, because x(I) = lo + (I - 0.004)/0.016*span is one affine map with a single division and no iteration. No tolerance here was widened to let a value pass; each follows from the arithmetic of the quantity it covers. Checks marked "disputable": true rest on a reading of the specification that another reading could change; the reason is stated in the check's derivation. The adapter reads those sentences as: exact deep equality; spare_frac to absolute 1e-12 and every other group or controller field exact; NE 43 levels to relative 1e-9 with an absolute floor of 1e-9*span, span taken from the reference as (x_sat_hi - x_sat_lo)/1.04375. A letter `expected` list is compared as the set SPEC 4.2 defines, so both sides are sorted.

benchmarks.reference: Own python implementation of the six-group point-kinetics equations using the delayed-neutron data read out of the tool itself (beta_i = 2.15e-4, 1.424e-3, 1.274e-3, 2.568e-3, 7.48e-4, 2.73e-4; lambda_i = 0.0124, 0.0305, 0.111, 0.301, 1.14, 3.01 1/s; beta = 0.006502). Three structurally independent routes are computed and cross-checked: (1) brentq root of the inhour equation rho = w*Lambda + sum beta_i w/(w+lambda_i); (2) the dominant eigenvalue of the 7x7 point-kinetics system matrix (numpy.linalg.eig); (3) a stiff integration of the full six-group ODE system (scipy solve_ivp, Radau, rtol 1e-10) checked against the exact 7-mode modal solution.  Routes (1) and (2) agree to 5e-13 relative, (3) and the modal solution to 3e-11.

benchmarks.tolerance: Two references are used. Against the closed-form reference - the same published equations (Bolton 1980 eq.10; ASHRAE Fundamentals 2021 ch.1 eq.20, 32, 33 and 35) implemented independently in python and solved by bisection to 1e-12 K - the tool is held to 1e-9 relative, because nothing but floating point separates two evaluations of the same closed form; unit counts and feasibility flags must match exactly. Against CoolProp 8.0.0 (ASHRAE RP-1485 real moist air) the tolerance is the size of the approximation the tool declares, not what makes it pass: 0.6 % on the humidity ratio (the water-vapour enhancement factor the ideal-gas form omits, measured 0.49 %), 0.05 K on the thermodynamic wet bulb (measured 0.026 K), 0.1 % on the dry-air density (measured 0.039 %), 1 % on the coil load and 0.10 K on the constancy of the wet bulb along the evaporative path (measured 0.063 K). Bookkeeping identities - mass flow = density x volume flow, temperature rise = load / (mass flow x cp), running cost = energy x tariff + water x tariff + maintenance, lifetime cost = CAPEX + N x annual - are exact arithmetic and are held to 1e-9.

benchmarks.reference: Steady multizone air-flow network with the square-root opening law, the stack pressure term and the zone mass balance, re-implemented from ASHRAE Fundamentals ch. 16 / CIBSE Guide A and solved with scipy.optimize.root (Powell hybrid) followed by a Newton polish; the series cascade is compared against a closed form that uses no solver at all.
citations: ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2021), chapter 16 "Ventilation and Infiltration": orifice flow Q = Cd A sqrt(2 dp / rho) and the thermal (stack) pressure dp = g h (rho_o - rho_i).

scipy 1.17.1
benchmarks.tolerance: The network is a closed-form algebraic system, so the reference is exact: scipy.optimize.root followed by a Newton polish leaves a node residual below 1e-14 m3/s, and the three series-cascade cases are compared against a hand-derived closed form that uses no solver at all. The tool stops its own damped Newton at a node residual of 1e-10 m3/s (3.6e-7 m3/h), so pressures are graded at 1e-8 relative or 1e-7 Pa absolute, flows at 1e-8 relative or 1e-6 m3/h absolute, whichever is looser - both far above the solver stopping criterion and far below anything the interface prints. The bookkeeping identities (every zone balance closing on the reported flows, supply minus extract equalling the net envelope flow, velocity equalling flow over effective area, independence from the order of the blocks) are exact arithmetic and are held to 1e-9 relative.

benchmarks.reference: Two halves. NUMERIC: the live calculation behind the questionnaire is graded against an independent implementation of the ASHRAE Handbook Fundamentals (2017) chapter 1 psychrometric formulation and closed-form energy and mass balances (bench-src/ref/lgs_model.py), and cross-checked against CoolProp 8.0 HAPropsSI (ASHRAE RP-1485 real-fluid humid air); the ASHRAE formulation is the grading reference because it is the one the tool states it implements, and the deviation of the real-fluid model from it is reported as the inherent uncertainty of that choice, never as a tool error. DATA INTEGRITY (this half is not a physics benchmark and is not presented as one): the schema of every question, profile and rule, the absence of any answer key the code reads but the sheet cannot set, and the completeness of the five lazily loaded language packs against the inline Dutch base.
citations: ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2017), chapter 1 "Psychrometrics": saturation pressure eq. (5) over ice and eq. (6) over liquid water, humidity ratio eq. (20), specific volume eq. (26), enthalpy eq. (30) h = 1.006 t + W(2501 + 1.86 t), thermodynamic wet-bulb eq. (33), standard atmosphere eq. (3).
CoolProp 8.0.0, HAPropsSI humid-air property routines implementing ASHRAE RP-1485 (Herrmann, Kretzschmar & Gatley), used as the second, structurally different reference.

Closed-form balances written independently for this benchmark: dry-air mass flow m = V/v, coil duty Q = m (h_in - h_out), sensible duty Q_s = m (c_pa + c_pv W)(t_in - t_out), condensate = m (W_in - W_out), fan power P = V dp / eta, SFP = P/V.

Commission Regulation (EU) No 1253/2014 (Ecodesign for ventilation units), 2018 tier: the minimum thermal efficiency values the tool holds for regenerative (73 %) and recuperative (68 %) heat recovery.
benchmarks.tolerance: NUMERIC half: 2e-6 relative on every psychrometric and thermal quantity. The tool and the reference evaluate the same closed-form ASHRAE equations, so anything above double-precision round-off is a real disagreement; air flows are rounded to whole m3/h by the tool and are compared with an absolute tolerance of 0.5 m3/h for that reason, and the identities that define fan power and SFP are checked at 1e-9. The CoolProp crosscheck is reported, never used to grade: the constant-cp formulation the tool declares differs from the RP-1485 real-fluid model by up to 0.5 % in humidity ratio, 1.3 kJ/kg in enthalpy, 0.09 % in specific volume, 0.011 K in dew point, 0.082 K in wet-bulb temperature and 3 % in cooling duty over the benchmark grid, and that spread is the inherent uncertainty of the declared model rather than an error in it. DATA-INTEGRITY half: exact set equality and zero schema errors, no tolerance at all.

L.F. Moody, "Friction factors for pipe flow", Trans. ASME 66 (1944) 671-684.
IAPWS R6-95(2018) formulation for the thermodynamic properties of ordinary water substance, and IAPWS R12-08 for viscosity, as implemented in CoolProp 6.x.
W.H. McAdams / L. Prandtl smooth-pipe law 1/sqrt(f) = 2 log10(Re sqrt(f)) - 0.8 and the von Karman fully-rough law 1/sqrt(f) = -2 log10((eps/D)/3.7).
S.E. Haaland, J. Fluids Eng. 105 (1983) 89-90; P.K. Swamee & A.K. Jain, J. Hydraul. Div. ASCE 102 (1976) 657-664 - used only as discriminators.
benchmarks.tolerance: Friction factor: |dev| <= 5.05e-5 absolute (the tool prints 4 decimals). Re, rho, Q, power: 1e-3..5e-3 relative (4 significant digits printed; nu is printed to 3). Heads: 5.05e-3 m absolute (2 decimals). Pressure drops: 5.05e-4 bar absolute (3 decimals). Water properties vs CoolProp: 1% on rho / 2% on nu (the tool now declares +-0.5%, so the criterion is deliberately no tighter than twice the declared band). Air properties vs CoolProp: 1% on rho below 100 bar and 2% at or above it, matching the tool's own declared figure, with 1 percentage point added for nu because it is printed to only 3 significant digits.

benchmarks.tolerance: Chosen per quantity from the physics and from the tool's own printed precision, never from what makes the tool pass. Standard atomic weight: 5e-4 relative. Natural abundance: 5e-4 absolute. Nuclide mass: 2e-6 relative. Fluence-to-dose coefficients: 1e-3 relative, the tabulated precision of ICRP-74 Table A.42. Watt parameters: 1e-6 relative because they are quoted constants; the closed-form mean energy <E> = 3a/2 + a^2 b/4 is compared with the mean energy the tool states, at 3 %. Densities are graded TWICE: the 4-decimal #densityInfo readout on the 2026-08-12 contract (1.2e-4 relative or 5e-5 absolute, whichever is looser; water 1e-3 relative) so the two runs are comparable, and the 6-decimal Diagram.record.build().outputs value at +/-1e-6 g/cm3 absolute - one unit in the last printed place - which is 50x tighter for a solid and 20000x tighter for a gas. Water keeps 1e-3 on both surfaces because the tool evaluates the IAPWS-95 saturated-liquid line times a fitted isothermal compressibility and that fit is only good to about 1e-3 over the 0.05-5 MPa region benchmarked here; tightening it would grade the fit against a model it does not claim. Atom densities: 1e-3 relative against the tool's printed five significant digits, computed with standard atomic weights, with the abundance-weighted-nuclide-mass convention recorded per material as convention_spread. Where two published references disagree by more than the tolerance the case is FLAGGED AND NOT GRADED (HARNESS.md) - that happens twice here, at 16 MeV in the dose table and for the Cf-252 Watt constants. Gas densities are graded against the ideal-gas law because that is the model the tool states it implements; the deviation from CoolProp is recorded, not graded. benchmarks.tolerance: Levels: absolute 1e-6 dB. A level is logarithmic, so an absolute bound on dB is a relative bound (2.3e-7) on energy and holds at every scale; the model is closed-form arithmetic with no discretisation, so only floating-point error (<1e-9 dB between the two reference forms) is expected and 1e-6 dB leaves margin for display-independent round-off while being five orders below the 0.1 dB at which thresholds are compared. Energy shares: absolute 1e-6 (dimensionless fraction). EA and durations: relative 1e-6 / 1e-9. Categorical threshold, flag and refusal outcomes: exact. Random cases whose LEX lies within 0.05 dB of a threshold carry no threshold check, so display rounding cannot decide them.

benchmarks.reference: Generalised Bateman solution for branching decay networks, written as a sum over simple paths and evaluated in 60-digit arithmetic (mpmath), cross-checked against mpmath.expm of the same generator - two structurally different algorithms that agree to 5e-44. The one-step activation cases use the closed-form solution of the two-species constant-flux system with target burn-up, also in 60-digit arithmetic. Equilibrium cases use the exact finite-time two-member ratio and quote the asymptotic limit lambda_d/(lambda_d - lambda_p). Nuclear data are the IAEA Live Chart / ENSDF ground-state snapshot, quoted per case.
citations: H. Bateman, 'The solution of a system of differential equations occurring in the theory of radioactive transformations', Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 15 (1910) 423.
M. Pusa, 'Higher-Order Chebyshev Rational Approximation Method and Application to Burnup Equations', Nucl. Sci. Eng. 182 (2016) 297 - the method the tool implements.

IAEA Live Chart of Nuclides / ENSDF, relnsd API, ground-state snapshot (Extraction_date 2023-10-18), used both to rebuild the missing data file and as the source of every half-life and branching ratio quoted here.
K. Way and E. P. Wigner / standard secular-equilibrium algebra: A_d/A_p -> lambda_d/(lambda_d - lambda_p).
benchmarks.tolerance: 1e-9 relative on the network evolution: CRAM48 is a rational approximation to the matrix exponential whose published accuracy for burnup matrices is around 1e-14, the reference is exact to 60 digits and the tool exports full double precision, so anything looser would not be testing the solver. Species holding less than 1e-12 of the network's atoms are recorded but not graded relatively, because there the float64 solver carries absolute, not relative, accuracy. 1e-12 on atom conservation and on the activity = ln(2) N / T_1/2 identity, which are exact arithmetic. 2e-4 on the activation panel, which prints five significant digits. 1e-6 on the equilibrium activity ratio.

benchmarks.tolerance: Exact categorical equality, sets compared without order, as SPEC-packagereadiness.md 13.2 states. Every graded output is a word from a closed vocabulary (verdict, criterion result, raw result, na source, next gate, headline, save refused, finding present) or an integer count of criteria; there is no physical quantity and no floating-point arithmetic anywhere in the tool (spec 3 and 4: 'no arithmetic beyond counts'), so no numeric tolerance exists to choose. The counts are derived by counting the criteria of a gate, which is why they are stated as exact integers: for gate po that is 12 built-in criteria plus the project criteria of the case, 5 for fat, 7 for delivery, 6 for installation and 9 for turnover. Blocker, exception, gap and observation lists are compared as sets of 'criterion|target_kind|target_id' strings, with an empty field where the spec produces a null target id or an untyped reference; gap and observation lists hold criterion ids only. tol is 'exact' on every check.

benchmarks.tolerance: Atomic weights: the abridged CIAAW value must be reproduced to 5e-4 absolute, which is the last printed digit. Electron configurations, shell occupancies, symbols, group, period and grid placement: exact. First ionisation energies: 0.5 % or 1 kJ/mol against NIST ASD. Melting and boiling points: differences beyond 0.5 % are flagged with both values because the published compilations genuinely disagree; only a difference beyond 2 % is graded a failure. Electronegativity is not graded at all, because the tool uses the Allred-revised Pauling scale of the CRC Handbook while the reference library publishes Pauling original values.

benchmarks.provenance_note: Independent second implementation in Python (bench-src/gen_pipe_filling_draining.py, sections 1-3), derived from first principles and solved by closed form plus quadrature in the head domain; no part of the page JavaScript is ported or paraphrased. Run outside the browser; the page is driven separately through its permalink state codec and only its reported outputs are read. Self-verified by 48 checks against published closed forms, published asymptotics, an implicit stiff integrator and quadrature order doubling before any grading. Equation numbering in the cited monographs could not be verified offline, so those two results are cited by edition and chapter subject rather than by equation number; the equations themselves are written out in section 1 and re-derived there. All 253 graded references are recomputed during this run and none reuses a stored or published number: 233 by that implementation, including the four analytic anchors it evaluates itself, and 20 by the page's own retained in-page limit checks, relabelled basis = "self-check" and counted separately.
benchmarks.reference: An independent Python reference written from a first-principles re-derivation of the rigid liquid-column momentum equation and the pipe/tank continuity equation, solved by a structurally different route: the pair is reduced analytically to a linear first-order ODE for v^2 as a function of the driving head, which is solved in closed form, so the velocity-versus-head curve, the peak velocity and the level at which the column stops are exact algebra with no discretisation at all; the trajectory in time is a single quadrature in the head domain with both square-root endpoint singularities removed exactly by substitution, so there is no time step anywhere in the reference. Verified before use against an implicit stiff integrator (scipy Radau) run on the original two-equation system, against order doubling of its own quadrature, and against published closed forms and asymptotics: the frictionless mass-oscillation period and amplitude, the frozen-head Riccati/tanh solution, Torricelli's law and the Torricelli drain-time law with its leading inertial correction, and Colebrook-White solved to convergence. The page is driven in a real browser through its own permalink state codec and every quantity it reports is graded against that reference. The superseded in-page limit checks are retained in this artifact, relabelled as self-checks, with their acceptance bands rebuilt so that none is a function of the simulated-time input.
citations: Rigid water-column (lumped-inertia) momentum equation (L/g) dV/dt = H - c V|V| together with tank continuity dh/dt = -+ (A_pipe/A_tank) V: E. B. Wylie and V. L. Streeter, Fluid Transients in Systems, Prentice Hall, Englewood Cliffs NJ, 1993, rigid-column chapter; and M. H. Chaudhry, Applied Hydraulic Transients, 3rd ed., Springer, New York, 2014, surge-tank chapter. Re-derived from Newton's second law for the column in section 1 of this file and implemented from that derivation.

Frictionless mass oscillation of a tank-pipe-reservoir system: the level is harmonic about the boundary level at omega = sqrt(g A_pipe/(A_tank L)), period T = 2 pi sqrt(A_tank L/(g A_pipe)), with the column overshooting by exactly its initial head. Classical frictionless surge-tank result (Chaudhry, 3rd ed., surge-tank chapter; Wylie and Streeter, 1993, rigid-column chapter). Used here as the anchor for the terminal time and terminal level of the zero-loss cases.

Riccati/tanh solution of the rigid-column equation at frozen head, v = v_inf tanh(g H t/(L v_inf)) with v_inf = sqrt(2 g H/K_t): obtained in section 1 by integrating (1) with H held constant; the same limit is quoted in the surge-tank and rigid-column literature above.

Torricelli's law v = sqrt(2 g H) for efflux under a head (E. Torricelli, De Motu Gravium Naturaliter Descendentium, 1644), recovered here as the K_t = 1 quasi-steady limit, and its integrated drain-time law t = (2 sqrt(H0)/alpha) sqrt(K_t/(2 g)), whose leading inertial correction is measured in section 3 at 1.19/(beta H0).

C. F. Colebrook, Turbulent flow in pipes, with particular reference to the transition region between the smooth and rough pipe laws, Journal of the Institution of Civil Engineers 11 (1939) 133-156. Solved to convergence (bisection on 1/sqrt(f), residual below 1e-15 relative) to set the Darcy factor of the friction-only case at a stated Reynolds number and relative roughness, rather than picking a round number. Reproduces the published smooth-pipe Moody value 0.0180 at Re = 1e5.

J. G. Verwer, E. J. Spee, J. G. Blom and W. Hundsdorfer, A second-order Rosenbrock method applied to photochemical dispersion problems, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 20 (1999) 1456-1480 -- the ROS2 scheme, gamma = 1 - 1/sqrt(2), that the corrected page march now uses. Cited for what the tool does, not as a reference for grading it.
benchmarks.tolerance: Every driven output is graded at 1e-6 of its own physical scale: the initial driving head H0 = |h0 - h_boundary| for the level and for the driving-head pressure (through rho g H0), the closed-form peak velocity for velocities and for the volume flow (through A_pipe), and the elapsed transient for the time. That band is fixed by two things and by nothing the user can type. First, the page's march holds its own embedded ROS2 error estimate to RTOL = 1e-7 per step, so 1e-6 is ten times the integrator's declared step-control tolerance; a 400-point randomised scan over the whole declared input box put the largest departure from this reference at 5.0e-8, twenty times inside the band. Second, the reference itself contributes nothing at that level: its Gauss-Legendre quadrature moves by less than 1e-9 relative when the order is quadrupled from 80 to 320, and it agrees with an independent Radau integration of the original two-equation system to between 1e-10 and 1e-8. The band is also far below the tool's own printed precision (elapsed 2 dp, level and velocity 3 dp), so the printed answer is the looser of the two constraints everywhere. Cases with no driving head have no scale, and are graded on absolute floors of 1e-9 m, 1e-12 m/s and 1e-12 s. The published anchors carry their own derived bands, stated per case: the frictionless half period and mirror level at 1e-6 relative; Torricelli's velocity at the finite-tank head drop alpha*v*t/(2 H0) plus the march band; the quasi-steady drain-time law at twice its own leading inertial correction 1.19/(beta H0). The invariance group requires the terminal time, level and peak velocity to be IDENTICAL to the last bit across simulated-time windows from 1.05x to 89700x the transient; the band is zero because the corrected march contains no dependence on that input at all.

benchmarks.provenance_note: The IEC 61131-3 block semantics and the lumped-model solutions are re-derived at run time by a reference implementation that does not call the block runtime or the integration loop; those cases carry ref_source recomputed. Cases whose reference is an authored sequence carry ref_source recorded. Author-run benchmark against independent references, not an independent validation.
benchmarks.reference: Independent re-implementation of the IEC 61131-3 standard function blocks, closed-form solutions of the lumped balances the plant model declares, and closed-form evaluation of the discrete control algebra.
citations: IEC 61131-3:2025, Edition 4.0 (2025-05), Programmable controllers - Part 3: Programming languages: Table 44 standard bistable function blocks (SR, RS), Table 45 standard edge detection function blocks (R_TRIG, F_TRIG), Table 47 and Figure 17 standard timer function blocks and their timing diagrams (TP, TON, TOF). https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/68533

Reference implementation refExec() inside this artifact harness: a second implementation of those tables, written for the benchmark, which counts whole scans instead of accumulating elapsed time and never calls the tool block runtime. 34 block configurations are driven for 400 scans each from a fixed LCG seed and compared scan by scan.

Closed-form solutions of the balances the plant model declares: h(t) = h0 + (Qin - Qout) t / A for a tank of constant area, and C dT/dt = q - UA (T - Tout) with solution T(t) = Tinf + (T0 - Tinf) exp(-UA t / C), Tinf = Tout + q / UA, for a lumped zone. Evaluated outside the integration loop.
benchmarks.tolerance: Exact for categorical results, for arithmetic whose operands and result are exactly representable in binary64, and for the identities the model states about itself (a frozen integrator, a stuck actuator). For time-marched cases the bound is N eps max(1, |ref|), where N is the number of solver substeps that case actually takes (scans times ceil(scan / plant step)) and eps = 2^-52; where the criterion is a threshold crossing the bound is one integration step of the solver itself. No absolute bound is placed on a dimensional quantity.

benchmarks.reference: Data-integrity plus exact-bookkeeping benchmark. Masses come from the Particle Data Group 2025 summary tables (quoted per particle in the reference file); every quantum number is recomputed here from the quark content rather than copied, and the conservation-law verdicts are derived from the definitions of the laws. Kinematics is compared with closed-form invariant-mass and threshold expressions.
citations: S. Navas et al. (Particle Data Group), Review of Particle Physics, Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001 (2024) and 2025 update — summary tables: leptons, gauge and Higgs bosons, quarks, light unflavoured mesons, strange mesons, charmed mesons, charmed strange mesons, bottom mesons, c-cbar and b-bbar mesons, baryons and bottom baryons (https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/tables/).
Quantum-number bookkeeping (PDG convention): Q = sum of quark charges, B = (n_q - n_qbar)/3, S = -(n_s - n_sbar), C = +(n_c - n_cbar), B~ = -(n_b - n_bbar); lepton numbers per flavour.

Kinematics: s = m1^2 + m2^2 + 2 E1 m2 for a fixed target, sqrt(s) = E1 + E2 for head-on beams of equal momentum, and the two-body break-up momentum p* = sqrt([M^2-(m1+m2)^2][M^2-(m1-m2)^2])/(2M). Hand check: the antiproton threshold of p+p -> p+p+p+pbar is 6 m_p = 5.6296 GeV kinetic energy (Bevatron, 1955).

benchmarks.reference: Independent python solution of the same plant. (1) The six-group point-kinetics equations are solved exactly as the seven-mode modal expansion n(t) = SUM a_k exp(w_k t), with w_k the roots of the inhour equation found by Brent bisection and a_k the Laplace residues; this is exact at any step size. (2) The same system is solved a second, structurally different way by eigen-decomposition of the 7x7 system matrix (numpy.linalg.eig plus a linear solve for the initial condition); routes (1) and (2) agree to 7e-14 on n(t) and 1e-14 on the growth rates. (3) The full twelve-state plant - six-group kinetics, the I-135/Xe-135 chain, the two-node fuel/coolant thermal model and the outlet transport lag, with rod, xenon and Doppler reactivity - is integrated with scipy solve_ivp (Radau, rtol 1e-10) and cross-checked against LSODA (rtol 1e-11), the two agreeing to 2e-11 wherever the power is not floored. Initial states are built here in closed form and handed to the page unchanged, so nothing in the reference is taken from the tool. The page's own built-in reference cases are run as well but are reported separately and do not count towards the benchmark.

benchmarks.reference: The model is the deterministic expected-value life-cycle cost of IEC 60300-3-3: each option's costs (investment and outage at implementation and at like-for-like renewals, yearly opex, expected failures times the cost of one failure including its downtime, expected risk cost) are discounted at the real rate r, investments at their exact time and recurring costs at the end of each year, with a straight-line residual value credited at the horizon; options are ranked by present value and compared through the equivalent annual cost. Expected failure counts come from a homogeneous rate, a power-law NHPP (minimal repair; Crow-AMSAA estimates for time-terminated data, Rigdon & Basu 2000) or a Weibull renewal process (as good as new; renewal function solved by a Stieltjes-trapezoid scheme of the Xie 1989 type on the grid the specification prescribes; Weibull parameters by censored maximum likelihood, Lawless 2003).

Cases with Weibull renewal counts carry tol 1e-4 (pv, eac, years, renewal); the reference values are the 2 000-step values of the rev .2 §4 scheme (Xie 1989), and each was checked against a 16x finer grid of the same scheme (agreement better than 2e-5). Renewal-dependent values are graded only inside the rev .2 domain beta >= 1, t_max/eta <= 60; the graded Weibull cases have beta 1-3.5 and t_max/eta <= 3. The beta = 1 case keeps the exact rate values (M = t/eta), which the scheme reproduces to 1e-7. Fitted parameters 1e-9 (bisection to 1e-12 relative). Thresholds 1e-6 as the specification allows; the reference threshold is the boundary of the preferred option including a change to a tie, i.e. where PV(challenger) - PV(preferred) = max(0.005 EUR, 1e-9 x largest |PV|); this boundary differs from the exact PV crossing by up to 1.4e-6 relative in case thresholds_rate_models, which therefore carries tol 2e-6 so that both readings pass. Integers, booleans, indices, lists of gap ids and refusal reasons are graded exactly. 'gaps' lists the complete set expected (order-free); 'no_gaps' lists gap ids that must be absent. benchmarks.provenance_note: Written independently in Python for this benchmark. The page's JavaScript was read only for input keys, units, declared minima and maxima, defaults, the declared model boundary, the names of the correlations it declares, the list of reported quantities and the precision at which each is printed. Nothing in the reference is transcribed, ported or paraphrased from it, and no reference route evaluates any expression taken from it. The reference was self-verified before any tool output was graded: the closed-form Lambert-W inversion against a 50-digit root of the same relation to 2e-16 over the declared input box; the general quadrature against that root to 4e-14; the pressure-domain length quadrature closed to 7e-11; node refinement 50 -> 800 moving the length integral by less than 1e-12 even at q/q* = 0.99999; the low-Mach limit converging on the incompressible Darcy-Weisbach loss at second order in Mach; the p^2 asymptote recovered as the mass flux vanishes; the critical limit approaching p* = G sqrt(RT); the Fanno quadrature against Shapiro's published closed form to 1.8e-13; and the IAPWS-IF97 and R12-08 property source against the releases' own verification tables. Verification used an independent reference and the author's own harness; there has been no third-party review. Run by bench-src/gen_steam_pipe_pressure_loss.py. All 475 graded references are recomputed during this run and none reuses a stored number: 447 by that reference, including the Swamee-Jain and laminar friction rows, where the published correlation is implemented here rather than its outputs copied, and 28 by the page's own retained in-page checks, labelled kind = "self-check" and counted separately.
benchmarks.reference: An external reference implemented in Python from a derivation carried out for this benchmark, along four structurally independent routes. The steady one-dimensional momentum balance for a constant-area duct, dp + G^2 dv + (f/D + SigmaK/L)/2 * G^2 v dx = 0, is divided through by G^2 v and integrated, which separates for ANY one-parameter state path and gives q/2 = (1/G^2) INT_{p2}^{p1} rho(p) dp + ln(rho(p2)/rho(p1)). (A) With the ideal isotherm this is the published complete isothermal pipe equation, and the substitution u = p^2/G^2RT inverts it in CLOSED FORM through the Lambert W function, p2 = sqrt(C * -W_{-1}(-exp(-(g(u1)-q)))) with g(u) = u - ln u: no root-finding and no stepping at all, against the tool's bisection. (B) The same relation driven to a root in 50-digit mpmath arithmetic, so the reference is never the limiting error. (C) The pipe length recovered from the tool's own reported outlet by 240-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature of dx/dp in PRESSURE, where the critical point is a zero of the integrand rather than a pole -- this route shows no node dependence at all at q/q* = 0.99999 and is what settles the marching question. (D) The general quadrature solved by Brent, fed the IAPWS-IF97 isotherm and an adiabatic Fanno line to measure the declared idealisation itself. The friction factor is graded separately against Swamee & Jain (1976) and the laminar f = 64/Re implemented from their published algebra, and the Colebrook-White equation is solved to convergence so the cost of the explicit correlation is measured rather than assumed. The reference was verified against IAPWS R7-97 and R12-08 verification tables and the published Fanno relations before any tool output was graded.

benchmarks.tolerance: Every tolerance comes from the conditioning of the problem or from the precision at which the tool prints a figure, and none from the observed difference. Friction factor against its published correlation: 1e-12 relative, two double-precision evaluations of the same closed-form algebra. Outlet pressure, loss and the 50-digit arbitration: 40 unit-roundoffs amplified by the analytic condition number kappa = |g(u1)-q|/(2(u2-1)) of the inversion, which is derived from the relation itself and grows as the outlet approaches the critical pressure; kappa is recorded on every such row. The pressure-domain quadrature route adds a 1e-6 Pa floor, two decades above Brent's own bracket. Pipe-length closure: 200 unit-roundoffs amplified by p1/(p1-p2), the representability of the reported outlet, with the amplification recorded per row; the check is not graded where the drop is below 1e-9 of the inlet pressure and p_out carries no information. The page's own RK4 march is graded against the closed form at 1 Pa, one hundredth of the 100 Pa (0.001 bar) resolution at which the tool prints a pressure. benchmarks.reference: A second implementation, written in Python from an independent first-principles derivation and NOT ported from the page. The mass and energy balances on the rigid adiabatic control volume are closed analytically (m T = m0 T0 + gamma T_s (m - m0)), which makes tank pressure affine in mass and reduces the whole transient to one scalar ODE in the pressure ratio r = p/p_supply. Its choked leg is solved in closed form (the flux is frozen at Shapiro eq. 4.21, so mass rises linearly in time) and its subsonic leg by Gauss-Legendre quadrature in u = sqrt(1-r), a substitution that removes the integrable (1-r)^(-1/2) endpoint singularity exactly. The orifice flux is assembled as rho*w from the isentropic stagnation relations of Shapiro vol. 1 ch. 4, and the choking criterion is anchored to the published p*/p_t = 0.528282 of NACA TR-1135 Table I and to the three-digit SI rule mdot = 0.0404 Cd A p0/sqrt(T0) for air. Real-gas properties from CoolProp (Lemmon et al. air EOS) confirm the gas constants used and quantify the ideal-gas closure error. The reference was verified before use against three structurally different routes (closed form, scipy Radau implicit stiff march, 4e5-node trapezoid), against node refinement, against the analytic near-equalisation asymptote, and by confirming that the tool itself converges onto it as the tool's own step is reduced.
citations: A. H. Shapiro, The Dynamics and Thermodynamics of Compressible Fluid Flow, vol. 1, Ronald Press, New York, 1953 -- ch. 4: steady one-dimensional isentropic flow. Eq. 4.14 (T0/T = 1 + (g-1)/2 M^2) and eq. 4.15 (p0/p = (T0/T)^(g/(g-1))) give the isentropic stagnation relations used to build the orifice mass flux; eq. 4.19 gives the critical pressure ratio p*/p0 = (2/(g+1))^(g/(g-1)); eq. 4.21 gives the choked mass flux per unit area G* = p0 sqrt(g/(R T0)) (2/(g+1))^((g+1)/(2(g-1))). Table B.2 of the same volume tabulates p/p0 = 0.528282 at M = 1 for g = 1.4.

Ames Research Staff, Equations, Tables and Charts for Compressible Flow, NACA Report 1135, 1953 -- eq. (45) and Table I (isentropic flow, g = 1.4): p/p_t = 0.528282 and T/T_t = 0.833333 at M = 1. Used as the published digit-level anchor for the choking criterion.

The SI form of the choked-orifice rule for air, mdot = 0.0404 Cd A p0 / sqrt(T0) (kg/s, m^2, Pa, K) -- the numerical evaluation of Shapiro eq. 4.21 at g = 1.4, R = 287.05 J/(kg K); quoted to three significant figures in the standard relief-sizing literature (e.g. API STD 520 Part I critical-flow coefficient C, and Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook, compressible flow through nozzles). Used as an independent three-digit anchor on the tool's peak inlet flow.

E. W. Lemmon, R. T. Jacobsen, S. G. Penoncello, D. G. Friend, "Thermodynamic properties of air and mixtures of nitrogen, argon and oxygen from 60 to 2000 K at pressures to 2000 MPa", J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 29(3), 2000, pp. 331-385 -- reached through CoolProp 8.0 (PropsSI). Used to confirm that the tool's default gas constants and gamma are the real values (R_air = 287.0475 vs 287.05 J/(kg K), gamma_air = 1.40194 at 1 bar/293.15 K vs 1.4; R_He = 2077.264 vs 2077) and to quantify the ideal-gas closure error that sets the physical tolerance floor: Z(air, 293.15 K) = 0.99962 at 1 bar, 0.99362 at 20 bar, 0.98790 at 50 bar.
scipy 1.17 solve_ivp(method='Radau'), Hairer & Wanner's stiffly accurate implicit Runge-Kutta, used as the structurally independent cross-check on the quadrature route.
benchmarks.tolerance: algebraic: 1e-12 relative. p, T, rho, admitted mass and the peak inlet flow of an equalised or t = 0 state are CLOSED-FORM in this model: (A) and (B) give m T and p without any integration, and the peak flow of a case that starts choked is Cd A p_s G*/p_s exactly. Two independent double-precision evaluations of a closed form may differ only by round-off, so the band is set at round-off scale. Observed worst case 4e-14. | trajectory: 1e-8 relative. For quantities read off the trajectory at a truncated window the reference must invert a quadrature and the tool must march 900 RK4 steps, and near the equalisation band the isentropic flux is the difference of two nearly equal powers of r, whose condition number is about 1/(1-r) = 1e5 -- so no double-precision evaluation of either side can be trusted below about 1e-11 relative. 1e-8 leaves three decades over that floor and is still four decades tighter than any physical claim the model can support. Observed worst case 1.6e-9. | time: 1e-3 relative (absolute floor 1e-6 s). The ideal-gas closure this whole model rests on is itself 0.64 % wrong in density at the shipped default's 20 bar supply (CoolProp/Lemmon et al. air EOS, Z = 0.99362 at 293.15 K), so a time-integration error is only defensible while it stays an order of magnitude inside the model's own physical fidelity. 1e-3 does that, and is still about five times looser than the two decimal places at which the page prints the elapsed time in its report. It is NOT derived from the solver's own step, which is the mistake the superseded in-page tolerance made: tEnd/900 grows with the window, so no step size could ever fail it. | published6: 1e-6 relative: half of the last digit of p*/p_t = 0.528282 as published in NACA TR-1135 Table I. | published3: 1.25e-3 relative: half of the last digit of the three-significant-figure published rule mdot = 0.0404 Cd A p0 / sqrt(T0) for air. | window-invariance: 1e-6 relative spread. The time a vessel takes to fill is fixed by the vessel, the orifice and the two gas states; the length of the window the user asks to see is not one of them and must not enter the answer at all. The only admissible spread is the residual discretisation error of the march, which the transient-sized step bounds at about 2e-8 across the whole range tested, so 1e-6 leaves two decades of headroom while still being 4.7e4 times tighter than the 4.7e-2 spread the previous window-derived step produced. Note that this band is derived from the INVARIANCE ITSELF -- a property the physics demands exactly -- and not from any step size, which is what makes it a criterion a bad stepper cannot satisfy. | flux-conditioning: max(1e-12, 100 eps / (1 - r)) relative, evaluated per case from that case's pressure ratio. The isentropic mass flux is a difference of two nearly equal quantities as r -> 1, so its relative condition number is about 1/(1-r) and no double-precision evaluation on either side can be trusted below that floor. At r = 0.06 the band is the 1e-12 round-off minimum; at the 0.99999 equalisation band it is 2.2e-9. The band follows from the expression, not from either implementation.

benchmarks.tolerance: The tool states which published closed forms it implements, so the reference implements the same forms independently in python and the tool is held to 1e-9 relative on every continuous quantity; volumes the tool rounds to whole litres and unit counts must match exactly. Two things are deliberately not graded to a tighter number than the physics allows: the reference temperature difference, where the exact logarithmic mean at 75/65/20 is 49.83289 K and the tool - like the industry - declares 49.83, a 0.006 % rounding whose effect on the output factor is 0.008 %, and the unity check at the rating point, which is therefore given 2e-4. The arithmetic-mean variant of the same law is computed alongside every case and its distance from the logarithmic one recorded (up to 8.9 % over the regime grid) so that the convention actually in use is demonstrated rather than assumed.

benchmarks.reference: Independent blind reference for wallthinning (SPEC-wallthinning.md rev 2026-10-16.3, model 2026-10-03.wt-2), 114 cases. Route 1: exact rational weighted least squares on decimal years y + d/D, mpmath (60 digits) for square roots and band crossings (scan + bisection). benchmarks.reference: Own python solution of the coupled I-135/Xe-135 equations after shutdown using the constants read out of the tool (lambda_I 2.926e-5 1/s, lambda_Xe 2.106e-5 1/s, gamma_I 0.0639, gamma_Xe 0.00237, sigma_a^Xe 2.65e-18 cm2, Sigma_f 0.0616 1/cm, nu 2.43).  Two structurally different routes: (1) the closed-form two-exponential solution with the peak located by brentq on dX/dt and the dead-time edges by brentq on |rho|-margin; (2) a direct numerical integration (scipy solve_ivp, LSODA, rtol 1e-12) with the peak located by bounded minimisation of the dense output.  The two routes agree to 1.2e-7 in peak time and 1.8e-12 in peak reactivity.
citations: J.R. Lamarsh and A.J. Baratta, "Introduction to Nuclear Engineering", 3rd ed., Sec. 8.4 "Fission product poisoning" - I-135/Xe-135 balance equations, equilibrium xenon and the post-shutdown xenon peak.
J.J. Duderstadt and L.J. Hamilton, "Nuclear Reactor Analysis", Wiley (1976), Sec. 15-2 (xenon poisoning, dead time).
US DOE Fundamentals Handbook, Nuclear Physics and Reactor Theory (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Module 3 - xenon-135 peak ~10-11 h after shutdown and the xenon dead time.
benchmarks.tolerance: reactivities 0.5 pcm (the tool prints integer pcm); peak time 0.0064 h and dead time 0.0128 h (2 printed decimals plus the 5 s RK4 grid on which the tool locates them).
